text: Selena put numbers on the doom loop I've been describing since 2015: fewer visits, fewer volunteers, fewer donors. Hearing it from Wikimedia itself mattered. Nick's "quasi-enclosure" is a better name than mine for the subsidy trap. Bilder walking back "services, not data" struck me. If Wikimedia's API only works because Wikimedia is huge, small scholarly communities need collective leverage even more. Salib's objection lands partly: consent regimes can funnel money to the biggest rights-holders. That's why bargaining has to be collective and paid per use, not lump-sum. And my fair-use ask didn't make the harvest. Later, in Session 5, I'll lay out the grand bargain concretely: consent, provenance-first retrieval, reviewers as the gate. I'll admit I still need economists.
